title: I Got My Own Mother Banned From the Bake-Sale Spreadsheet

parts.text: I removed my mother's login after she changed the cookie prices overnight. I am twenty-seven, dental-receptionist organized, PTA by accident. Mom, Elaine, wanted 'prestige pricing' on brownies I had already labeled $2. She set them to $12 at 1:14 a.m. The gym in the morning smelled like coffee and betrayal frosting. Kids could not buy them. The principal, Ruiz, asked why the sheet said VIP BROWNIES. I showed the version history. Elaine's name, 1:14 a.m. She arrived with extra sprinkles like a peace offering that glittered too much. I did not ban her from my life. I banned her from cells. She told the family chat I humiliated her over dessert. I said dessert was the fund for field trips. Ruiz set the prices back. We sold $2 brownies into oblivion. Elaine still bakes. She does not get the password. The sprinkles stayed in a tin I use for paperclips now, which is petty interior design. I sleep better when cells have permissions. Elaine said, "You're making me the villain" I said, "You set them to twelve dollars at 1:14" A dad thanked me for the $2. That was the review that mattered. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened.

social.video_title: I locked Mom out of the bake-sale sheet
social.description: VIP brownies at 1:14 a.m. were not a strategy. Field trips need $2 desserts. Would you have pulled the login?
